what_the_eye_sees: A domed half-round band covered all over in round gold pearls, with a small orange stone in a round bezel at the top. It is fuller than round 2: no bald metal, and the beads now grade from larger near the crest to finer toward the edges. It still reads as a caviar or granulation band, or a sea-urchin shell. The beads form rings around the bezel, so the stone reads as the urchin's boss and not as one bead in a spine. At 300 px the pattern is bead size alone. No forked crossbanding shows: the 0.12 mm step between high and low beads makes no shadow at this size, and in plain gold nothing else can carry the Gila's black and salmon bands. No dorsal bead line runs through the stone. In face-300, dull flat patches sit on either side of the bezel. The swell hardly registers, so the band looks like an even dome and not a fat tail. A jeweller would say 'granulated dome band with a citrine' and would not name a Gila monster or any lizard.
changes: Show the banding with a relief step that casts shadow, not with a 0.12 mm bead-height difference. On the shoulders and flanks (theta 35 to 145 and 215 to 325), raise the 'High beads' bands on a plateau 0.35 to 0.45 mm above the low-bead fields, or sink the low fields by the same amount. Use irregular transverse bands 3 to 5 beads wide that fork, merge and waver, with no straight edges and nothing radiating from the stone. The plateau edge can stay at a gentle slope for draft, but the step has to be at least 0.35 mm. Acceptance: in hero-300 you can count 4 to 6 crossbands on the visible flank, alternating shadowed and bright, and at least two of them visibly fork or join.

Replace the concentric bead rings around the bezel with a dorsal spine. Run one continuous line of domes along crest_v through the spessartite, at least 1.5 x the neighbouring beads and about 0.42 mm high, tapering away from 90 degrees. Bead right up to the spine on both sides so the flat, dull patches either side of the bezel in face-300 (about theta 75 to 105, off-crest) are gone. Acceptance: in face-300 a single horizontal bead line runs left to right through the stone, no ring or halo of beads circles the bezel, and no smooth patch wider than 2 bead pitches remains.

Make the fat-tail swell and the shingle-to-dome grade visible. Push the theta 90 key from width 1.22 / thickness 1.28 to about 1.35 / 1.42, keeping theta 35 and 145 at 1.08 / 1.10. Flatten the crowns within theta 90 +/- 40 into low, touching, slightly polygonal shingles with land at about 0.2 x pitch, and keep full round domes only in the outer third toward the edge fillets. Acceptance: in hero-300 the top of the band is clearly thicker than the flanks, and near the crest the beads read as tight tiles, not loose pearls.
